title: Projective scalar models under arbitrary coefficient change
statement:
Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be any morphism of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and set $R=\Lambda(*)$, $R'=\Lambda'(*)$. Let $S$ be any scheme, with small pro-étale site [sk-def-pe-site] and coefficient sheaves $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$, $\Lambda'_S=p_S^*\Lambda'$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use module sheaves, their ordinary unbounded derived categories, and ordinary uncompleted derived extension $P_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_S\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_S}P$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Scalar tensors mean constant sheaves [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model].

Suppose $P\in D(\Lambda_S)$ has a specified pro-étale cover $\{W_i\to S\}$ and isomorphisms $P|_{W_i}\simeq\Lambda_{W_i}\otimes_R P_i^\bullet$, with $P_i^\bullet$ bounded complexes of finitely generated projective $R$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Then $R'\otimes_R P_i^\bullet$ is bounded finite projective over $R'$, and in $D(\Lambda'_{W_i})$ there is an isomorphism
$$P_{\Lambda'}|_{W_i}\simeq\Lambda'_{W_i}\otimes_{\Lambda_{W_i}}(\Lambda_{W_i}\otimes_RP_i^\bullet)\simeq\Lambda'_{W_i}\otimes_{R'}(R'\otimes_RP_i^\bullet).$$
Each term of $\Lambda_{W_i}\otimes_RP_i^\bullet$ and of its new coefficient model is a direct summand of a finite free coefficient sheaf and is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; these bounded complexes are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The same assertion about flat terms and K-flatness holds for every bounded finite-projective scalar complex without any $P$ or covering assumption. No flatness of $R\to R'$, $\Lambda_S\to\Lambda'_S$, or the constant-to-coefficient ring maps is assumed.

proof.text: For each finite free scalar module, extension of scalars preserves its finite biproduct decomposition and sends the regular module to the regular module via Mod.regularExtensionIso. The same applies to finiteConstantScalarExtension, using preservation of finite colimits by the constant-sheaf inverse image. Map every given retract through these functors and compose with the finite-free comparison. This proves finite projectivity after scalar extension, including rank zero, without any flatness assumption on the ring map.

proof.text: The tensor unit is flat; finite biproducts of flat objects are flat; flatness passes to retracts. Thus the old and changed coefficient models have flat terms. The additive functors preserve zero terms, so both models and the changed scalar complex retain the given strict bounds. Apply the bounded-flat sublemma CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat in the source module of lem-sfb-bounded-above-flat-kflat to obtain the categorical two-sided K-flat predicates appearing in the Lean statement.

Invert this isomorphism to identify chart pullback of the derived extended object with derived scalar extension of the pulled-back object. This general comparison imposes no flatness assumption on the coefficient map.

proof.text: Apply derived extension on the chart to the specified local-model isomorphism. The old model is K-flat by the cover-independent assertion just proved. The left-derived-functor counit is therefore invertible on its homotopy-category image; conjugating by quotientCompQhIso identifies derived extension of its derived-category image with the image of termwise extension. Compose with the preceding chart comparison to obtain the first asserted isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality of the constant-sheaf adjunction counit gives the commutative coefficient square scalarCoefficientHom Λ X ≫ coefficientMap a X = scalarConstant.map(scalarSections.map a) ≫ scalarCoefficientHom Λ′ X. The adjunction mapMod comparison and comapMapModComapIso show that mapMod for scalarConstant commutes with scalar extension. Compose this comparison with extendScalarsComp and the coefficient-square equality to identify the two ordinary extension functors. Map this natural isomorphism to cochain complexes and then through DerivedCategory.Q. This proves the second asserted isomorphism; no projectivity or boundedness is needed for this last comparison.

lean.statement: theorem sfbPerfectScalarChangeModel (S : Scheme.{u}) (P : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ S))) (𝒰 : Scheme.Cover.{u} Scheme.proetalePrecoverage S) (C : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, CochainComplex (Mod Ab.{u + 1} (scalarRingObj Λ)) ℤ) (hb : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ l h : ℤ, (C i).IsStrictlyGE l ∧ (C i).IsStrictlyLE h) (hp : ∀ (i : 𝒰.I₀) (q : ℤ), ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (Retract ((C i).X q) (Mod.finiteFree (scalarRingObj Λ) n))) (e : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, (CondensedRing.upperStar Λ (𝒰.f i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj P ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbScalarModelComplex (𝒰.X i) (C i))) : ∀ i : 𝒰.I₀, Nonempty ((CondensedRing.upperStar Λ' (𝒰.f i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap a S)).leftDerivedFunctor.obj P) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbExtendedScalarModelComplex a (𝒰.X i) (C i))) ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbExtendedScalarModelComplex a (𝒰.X i) (C i)) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbScalarModelComplex (𝒰.X i) (sfbScalarChangedComplex a (C i))))
lean.note: The main theorem states the two derived isomorphisms on the specified cover.
